subtype: Teacher noticing yawning and short temper [Observer]
passage: Eshaan, when your Nani taught Class Four in Nagpur, the children called me Shalini Madam. There was a boy, Manoj, who always laughed first at my jokes. One winter he changed. He slumped over his desk, yawned through dictation and snapped at his bench-mate over a pencil. I nearly sent him out for not paying attention. Instead, at break, I asked him quietly how he was sleeping. He told me his family had moved into one room beside the railway line, and the night trains shook the walls. I spoke to his mother, who found him a corner away from the tracks, and I stopped marking him down for slow mornings. By spring his laugh was back.

qa.q: What shook the walls at Manoj's new home?
What was Shalini feeling when Manoj snapped over the pencil?
qa.a: She felt irritated enough to nearly send him out, but also puzzled, because he had always been so cheerful.

qa.q: What was the turning point in how Shalini handled Manoj, and why did it matter?
qa.a: Choosing to ask him quietly about sleep at break instead of punishing him; it uncovered the noisy trains, which a punishment would have hidden.

qa.q: What might that winter have been like for Manoj?
qa.a: He was probably worn out and cross from broken sleep, and being punished for it would have felt unfair.

grounding: Shows a teacher noticing a usually cheerful child turn slumped and irritable, and asking gently about sleep instead of punishing.

subtype: Teacher noticing yawning and short temper [Observer]
passage: The inspection team was due at eleven, and Raghav Sir wanted Class Three quiet and tidy. Tenzin, usually the first to wave good morning, sat slumped with his cheek on his fist, notebook unopened. When a classmate bumped his elbow, he growled, "Leave me alone!" Raghav felt the clock pressing on him; a punishment would be quicker. He crouched beside Tenzin anyway. "You seem very tired today. When did you get to bed?" Tenzin rubbed his eyes. "After tuition I had two worksheets. And my cousins were staying, so the TV was loud." Raghav let him start with the easier page and wrote in his diary for his parents: "Tenzin seems very tired. Can we talk about homework and bedtime?"

qa.q: When was the inspection team due?
Why was Raghav tempted to punish Tenzin?
qa.a: He felt pressured and anxious about the inspection, and a punishment seemed quicker than finding out what was wrong.

qa.q: What did Raghav do that helped, and what could come next?
qa.a: He asked kindly about bedtime and eased Tenzin in with an easier page; next, talking with the parents about homework and noise could fix the cause.

qa.q: How might the morning feel for Tenzin if he had been punished?
qa.a: He would likely feel misunderstood and more upset, and the real problem of late nights would stay hidden.

grounding: Illustrates a teacher under time pressure noticing a normally cheerful child's slump and temper and asking about bedtime, homework and noise.
